posts.hypothesis: Process breakdowns with a time stamp beat polished finals
posts.text:
This 6-second bottle shot took 41 hours.

Here's where every hour went:
thread: Hours 1-6: reference. 200+ frames of real liquid, slowed to 1/8 speed.
Hours 7-22: the sim. 14 versions. v9 looked right but read as fake at full speed.

Hours 23-41: light + comp. The light is what made it look expensive.

What part would you have cut?
alt_hooks: Clients see 6 seconds. We see 41 hours.
Why a 6-second 3D ad costs what it costs:

posts.hypothesis: Pricing takes drive replies from freelancers
posts.text:

replies.why: Big creative account, early, our core topic
options: AI replaced the cheapest 20% of our briefs. The other 80% got more expensive, because brands now want what AI can't fake: exact product, exact light, every frame approved.
We use both on every job. AI for the moodboard in an hour, 3D for the frame the client signs off on.
Every year something replaces 3D artists. We're still booked.
